governance_model.description: Description of the ownership and management structure (e.g., university-led, city-managed).

key_partners.description: A list of key partners, such as public health departments, universities, and technology vendors.

funding_sources.description: Primary sources of funding for the portal (e.g., foundation grants, institutional support).

sustainability_factor.description: Key factors contributing to the portal's long-term sustainability.

successful_portal_case_studies.description: Detailed analysis of successful local health data portals, specifically the Chicago Health Atlas and the NYC Environment & Health Data Portal. Each case study will cover its governance structure, funding model, key partnerships, sustainability factors, and community engagement strategies.

ownership_model.description: Common ownership structures for portals (e.g., university, city agency, non-profit).

data_stewardship_process.description: How data is refreshed, discrepancies are resolved, and indicator integrity is maintained.

funding_strategies.description: Typical funding strategies employed, such as grants, institutional budgets, or public-private partnerships.

community_governance_role.description: How community members or external stakeholders are involved in governance.

factors_in_portal_failure_or_discontinua.description: Analysis of common reasons why public health data portals fail or are discontinued, such as loss of funding, lack of institutional ownership, failure to engage the community, or outdated technology.

maternal_health_portal_landscape.description: An assessment of whether any US city has built a unified maternal health data portal that consolidates VDH, Census, and CDC sources into a single race-disaggregated view. It will describe existing city-level maternal health dashboards and compare their features and outcomes to the user's specified model.

per_indicator_citations.description: Whether the dashboard provides specific citations for each data point or indicator.

methodology_documentation.description: How methodology is documented and made accessible (e.g., 'methodology cards', 'about the data' pages).

data_vintage_labeling.description: Indicates if the dashboard clearly labels the time period and last update for the data.

suppression_policy_disclosure.description: Whether the portal explicitly discloses its rules for suppressing small numbers.

suppression_threshold.description: The number below which data is suppressed (e.g., counts fewer than 10).

data_types_affected.description: The types of data that are suppressed (e.g., counts, rates, population figures).

rationale.description: The stated reason for the suppression policy.

guidance_for_local_data_suppression.description: Recommendations for how local health data portals should implement small-number suppression policies, drawing from the CDC WONDER model and other best practices to balance data utility with privacy protection.

national_underestimation_rate.description: The approximate national percentage of underestimation for AI/AN mortality.

cause_of_misclassification.description: The reason for the underestimation (e.g., incorrect race reported on death certificates).

authoritative_source.description: The primary source of this data (e.g., NCHS, specific studies).

misclassification_impact_on_richmond_dat.description: An analysis of whether the national AI/AN mortality underestimation likely affects Richmond-specific data. This will discuss the prevalence of the issue and the probable impact in the absence of a specific local study for Richmond, VA.

portal_guidance_for_surfacing_data_cavea.description: Actionable recommendations for how a public health data portal should surface important data limitations and caveats, such as the AI/AN misclassification issue, to ensure users interpret the data correctly.

key_recommendations_for_portal_developme.description: A summary of actionable recommendations for organizations looking to build or maintain a successful public health data portal, based on the findings of the report.

platform_options.description: Discussion of platform choices, such as open-source (e.g., Django, Drupal) vs. proprietary.

development_methodology.description: Recommended development approaches like agile development and modular contracting.

data_access_and_apis.description: Importance and implementation of APIs, data feeds, and other methods for programmatic data access.

architecture_for_sustainability.description: Architectural decisions that support long-term maintenance and incremental updates.

source_name.description: Name of the data source (e.g., CDC WONDER, US Census, PRAMS).

description.description: A brief description of the data source.

example_indicators.description: Examples of health or social indicators derived from this source.

common_data_sources_and_indicators.description: A list of common data sources (e.g., Vital Statistics, Census, CDC, PRAMS, local surveys) and types of health and social indicators typically featured in public health data portals.

community_engagement_strategies.description: An overview of strategies that successful portals use to engage with community members, researchers, and policymakers to ensure the portal remains relevant, trusted, and utilized.
